Turn a DNA strand into its RNA complement: G to C, C to G, T to A and A to U.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/rna-transcription) (MIT). Listed under [Encoding & Ciphers](/examples/?subject=encoding-and-ciphers).

```nomi-run
// FILE: rna_transcription.nomi
//# Transcribes a DNA strand to its RNA complement.

/// The RNA complement of a DNA strand: G to C, C to G, T to A and A to U.
/// A strand holding anything but those four nucleotides is an error.
pub fn to_rna(dna: String) -> Result<String, String> {
    dna
    |> Iter.map(complement)
    |> Result.collect()
    |> Result.map(String.join)
}

fn complement(nucleotide: String) -> Result<String, String> {
    case nucleotide {
        "G" -> Ok("C")
        "C" -> Ok("G")
        "T" -> Ok("A")
        "A" -> Ok("U")
        _ -> Err("invalid nucleotide '${nucleotide}'")
    }
}

// FILE: rna_transcription_test.nomi
import rna_transcription.to_rna

test "transcribes DNA to RNA" {
    cases = [
        #("Empty RNA sequence", "", ""),
        #("RNA complement of cytosine is guanine", "C", "G"),
        #("RNA complement of guanine is cytosine", "G", "C"),
        #("RNA complement of thymine is adenine", "T", "A"),
        #("RNA complement of adenine is uracil", "A", "U"),
        #("RNA complement", "ACGTGGTCTTAA", "UGCACCAGAAUU"),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, dna, expected), description {
        assert to_rna(dna) == Ok(expected)
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- `to_rna` returns `Result<String, String>`, though the canonical data has no
  error case. A character other than the four nucleotides has no complement,
  and the alternatives were a wrong answer or a trap. The tests compare with
  `Ok(expected)`.
- The nucleotides stay one-letter Strings matched by a `case`, not an enum.
  An enum would need a parse step and a render step around a four-arm table
  for no gain in a function this size.
- `Result.collect` turns the per-nucleotide results into one, so the first
  invalid nucleotide becomes the error.
- The parts are joined with `Result.map(String.join)`: where a function of
  one parameter is expected, `String.join` takes its default separator.
